name: net.diofis/babelii
title: Babelii-Diofis
description: Buy phone credit, data packages, PLN tokens, bills and game vouchers in Indonesia via an AI agent.

tools.name: discover_babelii
tools.description: Discover Abel, available commerce scopes and the verified origin of this MCP connection.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search orderable platform products (default 10 rows, limit up to 20; a 'more' note means the page was full; one call is enough: every orderable row states price, requires_destination, needs_inquiry and open_denom as true/false). needs_inquiry=true means a bill or destination check is required first (BPJS, PDAM, PLN postpaid, e-wallet top-up; such rows often have price_type=open because the amount comes from the inquiry): prepare_purchase runs it for you. open_denom=true means the BUYER states the amount (amount parameter, min Rp1,000, for example an e-wallet top-up); the two are independent. A row with available=false and sold_out=true is a real product whose stock is empty right now: say so, never order it, it carries no ref. catalogue is a group key from the platform capability list (catalogue_groups, returned by discover_babelii), e.g. phone-credit, data-voucher, data-package, token, game, bills; omit it when unsure. A range such as 1-3 days means min_validity_days=1 and max_validity_days=3. Sort: relevance, price_asc, value_per_gb_day. For a voucher without a target number use data-voucher and requires_destination=false. Missing coverage/operator must not be guessed.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Optional: full details of one product by a ref from search_products (search rows already carry what is needed to buy).

tools.name: search_marketplace
tools.description: Browse the Babelii Marketplace, where other vendors sell hotspot vouchers, food, services and goods (the same listings as the /marketplace page). Use it when the buyer asks what the marketplace has or names a vendor or a kind of item (for example "makanan", "voucher hotspot", "jasa"); an empty query lists a sample. Read only: stocked hotspot vouchers are ordered like any product (search_products then prepare_purchase), every other listing is bought on its buy_url page, so give the buyer that link. Rows with sold_out=true are real vendor products whose stock is empty right now. The result also carries buy_requests: open requests where buyers say what they are LOOKING FOR (title, kind, quantity, budget, link; never buyer names or contacts). "Barang yang sedang dicari" means buy_requests, not the vendor listings. Each listing has order_via, which says how to buy it: 'search_products ...' means a stocked voucher you can order through search_products (search its title) then prepare_purchase, or the buyer can use buy_url; 'buy_url ...' means only the buy_url page (give the link, do not try prepare_purchase). buy_requests are buyers' wishes that vendors can answer at buy_requests_url, NOT things for sale, so never offer to buy one.

tools.name: ask_abel
tools.description: Consult Abel (AI Assistant Babelii), Babelii's business adviser, for unclear needs or product selection. Bounded model use; returns catalog recommendations, never places an order. Use direct search when filters are known.

tools.name: prepare_purchase
tools.description: Prepare an expiring, actor-bound intent without placing an order or debiting money. For products that need an inquiry this call runs the inquiry itself (no separate inquire_purchase needed). For identities WITHOUT an account (anonymous agents) buyer_name is REQUIRED; buyer_phone and buyer_email are optional and must never be demanded from the user. An account-bound identity buys as its account and needs none of them. An anonymous order is paid through the payment link returned by execute_purchase: give that link to the buyer and tell them fulfilment starts after payment. Show the returned destination, customer name (if any), product and amount to the user. Products with open_denom need amount (nominal typed by the buyer, min 1000); products with needs_inquiry need the inquiry_id returned by inquire_purchase for the same destination and amount. Fixed-price products in some groups return their native checkout form. The result carries a policy block: how long the intent is valid (expires_at, about 5 minutes), how many renewals remain, and the per-order and hourly limits of this identity. An order refused for a limit is final: do not split it, retry it or look for a way around it; tell the buyer plainly.

tools.name: inquire_purchase
tools.description: For products with needs_inquiry (bills, e-wallet top-ups): look up the customer name and amount the buyer must confirm. Rate-limited like the web form and may cost the platform an upstream lookup, so call it once per request and only after the buyer gave the destination. Returns an inquiry_id for prepare_purchase; the lookup result is stored server-side, never trust or resend raw data.

tools.name: execute_purchase
tools.description: Place the prepared order only after explicit user confirmation of details and terms. Requires orders.execute scope; identity determines payment authority. Retrying the SAME intent never authorizes another order. Do not replace an indeterminate intent with a new one. Payment: omit pay_with to use the default shown in the prepared summary (payment.default). Pass pay_with (gateway, cash or coin) and, for gateway, channel only when the buyer chose a method that appears in payment.options; a method that is not listed is refused.

tools.name: purchase_status
tools.description: Pass exactly ONE of intent_id, order_number, order_id or track_url (two or none is refused). Use intent_id right after execute_purchase, order_number or track_url for a guest order. Any guest can check coarse status using their order_number. A full track_url from checkout unlocks guest details across sessions; never invent or fetch a tracking URL. An account or internal connection can use its own order_number or order_id. intent_id remains supported. Order creation is not delivery success.

tools.name: renew_purchase
tools.description: Requote an unexecuted intent without another order or debit. Supply its current quote_version (initially 1). Returns the same intent_id, a new quote_version and up to five more minutes, at most three renewals within thirty minutes. Show the latest price/details and ask for confirmation again; execute with the returned version. Retrying the same input returns the saved renewal. Expired paid inquiries are not repeated automatically.
